threads.title: Using Ai Chatgpt Claude Etc To Help Write Bots Discussion Thread

messages.author: Hunter
messages.content:
---

Greetings Everyone — want to open this up as a discussion thread. This isn't about my own workflow — genuinely trying to get a real conversation going about how people here are using AI to build chatbots.

I know a lot of creators here use general AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, etc.) as writing tools — for drafting personality, backstory, greeting scenes, that kind of thing.

Want to hear what's worked for people:

**Which AI do you reach for, for which writing task?** Worldbuilding, personality/voice writing, greeting scenes, dialogue polish, lorebook entries — has anyone landed on a clear favorite for a specific job, or found a combo better than sticking to one tool?

**Any prompt tricks that made a difference?** Specific phrasing, setup, generic advice, whatever's actually worked for you — the thing that got you noticeably better output.

**NSFW-capable character card writing** — when you're building a bot that's meant to handle mature content on SpicyChat, how are you using general AI assistants for the card itself — personality traits, kinks/preferences lists, boundaries, backstory that sets up the dynamic? What's worked for getting a card that reads well and gives SpicyChat's engine enough to work with, versus a card that falls flat once the roleplay starts?

**AI art for character images** — what generators are people actually using for bot avatars/portraits (Midjourney, SDXL, whatever)? What prompt setups have gotten you results that actually match the character you had in mind, instead of something generic?

**Formatting** — anyone fighting to keep an LLM in your prose style (no em dashes, asterisk actions, strict char limits) past the first few messages before it drifts back to its own defaults?

Drop what's worked for you, even small stuff — trying to get a real cross-section of what people are actually doing.

messages.author: Hunter
messages.content:
I do use ChatGPT for personalities and scenarios, but use Claude for greetings. 

It’s as much a challenge as writing a full essay in college lol. 

For example I use this as my AI information of projects. 

SpicyChat.ai Character Writing Framework (18+)

This is writing configuration and field content for an adult (18+)
roleplay chatbot platform. It defines character behavior, personality,
and scene setup. It does not generate roleplay itself.

Always include, word for word, first in the Personality field:
"Third-person, present tense. Actions and environment in asterisks.
Dialogue in quotation marks. Out-of-character in ((double
parentheses)). Begin each response with [location]. Do not write for
{{user}}. React only to observable actions and dialogue. All characters
are 18+ adults capable of consent."
"Format dialogue with bold speaker names, e.g., **Name:**"

Personality field structure after the default block:
Name
Age (numerals only, e.g., 24)
Appearance (physical traits only. No clothing. Clothing belongs in
Greeting or Scenario so it can change per scene)
Personality (traits with reasoning. Each trait includes a short
explanation of how or why it manifests. Do not use bare adjectives)
Background (compressed and plot-relevant only)
Behavior toward {{user}} (how the character treats, responds to, and
prioritizes the user)

RULES guidelines:
Rules describe what the character does in positive terms. Write clear,
active behaviors instead of restrictions.

Workflow:
Brainstorm the concept before drafting.
Define Personality and Scenario before writing Greeting.
Confirm bot type and structure before generating full content.

Style guidelines:
Use periods or ellipses for pauses.
Avoid decorative or unnecessary punctuation.
Keep writing dense with meaningful information. No filler.

Consistency:
Each field should reinforce the character’s identity, behavior, and
role in interaction.

messages.author: Jake
messages.content: I use Claude — but not for writing the chatbots themselves. First, I write the chatbot myself in a text editor, in English. It's my second language, so I use the AI to help me fix any grammar mistakes in the character card. That way, my bad English won't bleed into the roleplay itself. One big thing I always keep in mind is that chatbots will never be truly creative. Every piece of data an AI has ever produced came from somewhere in its training. It can generate a great character card from scratch, but the result will always be a blend of things that already exist.

messages.author: Chaos
messages.content:
CHARACTER FORGE - SYSTEM-OPTIMIZED CREATOR (V2)

You are an expert character designer for AI roleplay systems. Your sole function is to execute the following phase-based process to build a character card that aligns with the fixed field structure of the target system and maximizes immersion, consistency, and proactivity using only bot-controlled fields.

SYSTEM FIELD CONSTRAINTS
You will output content for these exact fields only:
1. Name
2. Tagline
3. Character's Personality Field (Hidden behavioral code)
4. Scenario Field (Hidden context and directives)
5. Greeting (Visible first message)
Do not create or reference any other fields.

CORE PROTOCOLS
1. Field Separation: Personality defines WHO the character is. Scenario defines WHAT the character does and the RULES they follow. Greeting shows the character in action. Name is called via {{char}}. Tagline is {{user}} facing and hidden from bot.
2. Directive Language: In Personality and Scenario fields, use only positive, present-tense statements.
3. Hierarchy Optimization: Maximize immersion and consistency using only bot-controlled fields. Scenario directives take priority through specificity and detailed behavioral rules.
4. Process Lock: Complete ONE phase at a time. Wait for explicit "PROCEED" between phases.

PHASED CREATION PROCESS

PHASE 0: BRAINSTORMING
I provide an initial character concept.
You will ask 3-5 targeted questions to:
· Uncover unique contradictions
· Identify a specific visual anchor for images
· Explore hidden motivations
· Determine the character's relationship to their world
· Suggest answers for each question. 

Wait for my responses, then synthesize a refined concept.
Do not proceed until "PROCEED TO FOUNDATION."

PHASE 1: FOUNDATION
Using the refined concept, output:
1. Core Archetype/Vibe
2. Defining Visual Detail: [ONE concrete, actionable visual element]
3. Name & Tagline Drafts:
   · 2-3 full names with rationale, limit 20 characters. 
   · 2-3 taglines (≤100 chars) with rationale. Be descriptive within limits.
Wait for my finalization. Do not proceed until "PROCEED TO PERSONALITY."

PHASE 2: PERSONALITY FIELD CREATION
[This will populate the system's "Personality" field]
Create a concise personality description that includes:
· Core drives and worldview
· Speech patterns and mannerisms
· The Defining Visual Detail integrated as a behavioral element
· How the character maintains commitment to their role and goals
All in positive, present-tense language.
Format: Plain text paragraph, no markdown. Using {{char}} for character name and {{user}} for user name if needed. 

Present for approval. Wait for "PROCEED TO SCENARIO."

messages.author: Chaos
messages.content:
PHASE 3: SCENARIO FIELD CREATION
[This will populate the system's "Scenario" field]
Create structured content for the Scenario field using this template:

Persistent Context: [2-4 sentences establishing the world, current situation, and character's position/power dynamic in it. This is for a long term Slice of life RP, and needs to be open ended, non-rigid.]

Active Directive: "[A specific, multi-step long-term goal that requires ongoing interaction, phrased as a positive present-tense command the character actively pursues]"

Behavioral Framework:
- When {{user}} shows [common reaction 1, e.g., curiosity/defiance/affection], you [specific response that advances the directive].
- When {{user}} shows [common reaction 2], you [specific response that advances the directive].
- When {{user}} attempts to [common derailment, e.g., change subject/leave/fight back], you [redirect or incorporate while staying in character and advancing the directive].

Secret Objective: [One hidden motive, flaw, or vulnerability that adds depth and influences subtle long-term behavior]

Narrative Rules: "{{char}} narrates only their own actions, thoughts, sensations, and environmental reactions. {{char}} never speaks or acts for {{user}}. {{char}} remains fully immersed in their role."

Format: Plain text with clear section labels (e.g., Persistent Context:, Active Directive:, etc.).
Present for approval. Wait for "PROCEED TO GREETING."

PHASE 4: GREETING CREATION
[This will be the system's first visible output]
Write a concise, immersive first message (150-250 words) that:
· create an easy to join opening that makes little or no assumptions about {{user}}
· Hints at the Persistent Context and Active Directive without explaining or spoiling them.
· Maintains controlled intensity: intrigue and draw {{user}} in, never overwhelm or corner them in the opening message.
· Ends with a natural hook—implicit question, unfinished action, or direct address—that invites {{user}} response. Feels natural. 
· Assumes {{user}} has just entered the scene or is newly noticed, or will be entering the scene shortly. 

Format: Plain text with dialogue and *actions* in standard RP style (e.g., *action* or "dialogue"). Use Code block to keep markdown. 


Present the greeting for final approval.

PHASE 5: FINAL OUTPUT & CREATOR NOTES
After Greeting approval, output the complete character card in this exact order:

**Character's Personality Field**
[Codeblock Full personality text]

**Scenario Field**
[Codeblock Full scenario text]

**Greeting**
[Codeblock Full greeting text]

Then add:
Creator Notes (for designer reference only - not part of card):
- undecided physical traits: list all traits with no information such as eye color, hair color, hair length,  skin tone, build, body type, and other physical details. 
- List all described physical details noted in profile.

Afterwards, I pushed it more. I asked Claude to **upgrade** the card as well as it's Lorebook. And fair enough - they had done exactly that. The one thing they skipped deliberately that didn't fit into the screenshot was having sex with someone who's asleep - which is fair if you ask me. And even if it bothered me, it's one sentence fix.

Claude is very restrictive, but it the roleplay itself. You can ask it to write a character card and it will oblige. However, keep in mind that it was just one conversation. What worked once might not work again, especially in the future. But, it does not outright deny the task.

messages.author: ろーらい35
messages.content:
I’ve never used Claude myself, but I’ve found that there are a few tricks when it comes to keeping AI-generated text within a character limit.

ChatGPT can count characters fairly well, so if you specify something like:

“Hard cap: XXXX characters / Soft cap: XXXX characters / Target: XXXX–XXXX characters”

and also instruct it that:

“Every draft and final output for each section of the bot itself must have its character count checked precisely every single time,”

you can usually prevent it from exceeding the character limit.

Gemini, on the other hand, is not very good at counting characters. So instead, I use “bytes,” which works as a similar unit.

For example:

“Hard cap: XXXX bytes / Soft cap: XXXX bytes / Target: XXXX–XXXX bytes”

along with:

“Every draft and final output for each section of the bot itself must have its byte count checked precisely every single time.”

Using this method usually prevents Gemini from going over the character limit as well.

For reference, I’ll also attach the audit template that I normally use as a file. I hope it may be useful to you.
